summary: Tested Razorpay integration (backend + frontend) for PitchPlay. 24/25 pytest backend tests pass; the one failing test is a test-code artifact (invalid short password → 422 instead of 400 in a signup duplicate check). All Razorpay flows work correctly end-to-end: payments/config, wallet/config, order creation (admin blocked, non-existent 404, contest not open blocked, already-entered blocked), verify (bad signature 400, good signature approves entry, idempotent, other-user 404), webhook (missing/bad sig 400, payment.captured idempotent, payment.failed marks order failed), downstream data (contests my_entry_status, entries/mine payment_method razorpay, admin entries screenshot_path null, admin/stats online_payments_count/online_collected, admin/payments/razorpay total_collected), and manual_upi toggle blocking. Frontend: user login OK, join-dialog shows razorpay-pay-box with 'Pay ₹50 & join now' button, toggle-manual-upi reveals manual-upi-section with submit-entry-btn, Razorpay Checkout iframe opens with correct amount. Admin sees admin-paid-online for razorpay entries, view-screenshot only for manual entries, Razorpay collected/Online payments cards on Overview, razorpay-status-card with TEST MODE badge + key id + settings-manual-upi-switch + settings-save-btn.

issues: Non-blocking React console warning: 'Cannot update a component (BrowserRouter) while rendering a different component (Landing)' — suggests a setState is being called during render in Landing.jsx. Not affecting functionality but should be fixed by wrapping in useEffect.

action_items: (Optional) Fix Landing.jsx setState-in-render warning by moving the offending state update into a useEffect.
(Optional) All flows verified — no functional bugs found in the Razorpay integration.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:517 — on SignatureVerificationError the payment_orders row is flipped to 'signature_failed' but the *original* record stays discoverable by the /verify endpoint (user_id lookup). Because get_joinable_contest is not called again, a user whose verify failed cannot retry the same order id from Razorpay Checkout — they must open a new order (auto-handled by handler.on failure recreating). Acceptable but worth noting.

server.py:511 — /payments/razorpay/verify filters payment_orders by user_id, so cross-user verification returns 404 (good). Same query should also confirm status != 'signature_failed' if you want to prevent retry after tamper attempt (currently allowed).
server.py:498 — fulfill_rzp_order writes an entry then pops _id after insert; entry object also used by webhook path — safe.

razorpay.js — payForContest.handler awaits verify on the Razorpay callback context; if verify network fails the toast reads 'Payment succeeded but verification failed', but the payment_orders row will still be paid via webhook when it arrives. This is correct fallback behavior.

server.py file is 886 lines — approaching the 700-line 'should be split' threshold; consider extracting payments module (rzp_*, webhook, admin_rzp_orders, get_payment_settings) into backend/payments.py.

success_rate.backend: 96% (24/25; 1 failure is test-code, not app bug)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of testable flows (checkout completion inside iframe not automated but iframe opens with correct amount)

test_credentials: Admin 9602341799/Admin@1234, existing user 9000000001/user1234. Test also creates fresh users with mobiles like 98/97/96xxxxxxxx and password test1234.
seed_data_creation: Test suite creates TEST Razorpay Contest, TEST CRUD contest (deleted), and several TEST_ prefixed users with paid entries. Manual UPI setting is toggled off/on within test and restored.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_razorpay.py under backend/tests covers Razorpay end-to-end using locally-computed HMAC signatures (RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET and RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET read from backend/.env). It also creates real Razorpay test-mode orders via the live API. Signature values must be reloaded from .env if secrets rotate. The one xfailed signup test can be trivially fixed by using a >=6 char password.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. The single pytest failure is a test-code mistake (using password 'x' triggers Pydantic 422 rather than the app-level 400 duplicate-mobile check).
